name: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator
title: AiThinkingIndicator
wrapsNative: TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval:)) with Text and a LinearGradient foreground; MonarchAiBotGlyph; AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: The "Thinking…" state before an assistant's first token, with a soft shimmer or a pulsing assistant mark and, after a few seconds, the elapsed time.
whenToUse: After a message is sent and before the reply streams its first token, or while a named tool or retrieval step runs ("Searching your files…").
whenNotToUse: Once text streams, show the text. In a dock or row with no room for a label, use MonarchAiTypingDots. For loading that is not the assistant, use the standard ProgressView (see spinner).
api: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator.init(label: String? = nil, startedAt: Date? = nil, variant: MonarchAiThinkingIndicatorVariant = .shimmer, showsElapsedAfter: TimeInterval = 3, isAnnounced: Bool = true, elapsedLabel: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Thinking…", for example "Searching your files…".

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the assistant started working. The moment the indicator first appeared when nil. Pass it when the view can be rebuilt during one turn.

options.name: variant
options.description: shimmer: a band of the assistant colour sweeps across the label. mark: a pulsing assistant mark before a still label.

options.name: showsElapsedAfter
options.description: Seconds before the elapsed time appears. .infinity never shows it.

options.name: isAnnounced
options.description: Whether VoiceOver announces the label when the indicator appears and when the label changes.

options.name: elapsedLabel
options.description: Formats whole elapsed seconds. By default the narrow unit format of the environment's locale ("5s", "1m 5s").

states.name: thinking
states.description: The label, with the shimmer or the pulsing mark.

states.name: long wait
states.description: After showsElapsedAfter seconds the elapsed time follows the label and updates every second.

states.name: Reduce Motion
states.description: The shimmer and the pulse stop; the label is muted text and the mark is still. The clock still ticks once a second.

appearance: The label is muted text; the shimmer band and the mark use the assistant (ai) strong colour; the elapsed time is subtle text with tabular figures. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web shimmers a band of the thinking tint behind the label; iOS sweeps the assistant colour through the label's own text, which keeps contrast in every theme. The web announces through a hidden live region; iOS posts an announcement. Android uses the same names. The parity map named ai-typing-dots as the mark; the web component uses the assistant bot mark, so iOS reuses MonarchAiBotGlyph (from ai-generated-badge) and leaves the dots to MonarchAiTypingDots for places without a label.
accessibility: One element read as the label, with the elapsed time as its value and the updates-frequently trait.
The label is announced when the indicator appears and again when the label changes; the elapsed time is never announced.
The mark is decorative and hidden.
Under Reduce Motion the shimmer and the pulse stop.
The label wraps at large text sizes; nothing has a fixed height.
edgeCases: A startedAt in the future counts as 0 seconds.
The clock restarts if the view is recreated without startedAt.
Long labels wrap and the elapsed time stays after them on the same baseline where it fits.

examples.title: A named step with a pulsing mark
examples.code: MonarchAiThinkingIndicator(label: "Searching your files…", startedAt: start, variant: .mark)
